verses.text: Paul and Timothy, servants of Christ Jesus, to all God's holy people in Christ Jesus at Philippi, including your leaders and servants:
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I thank my God every time I think of you.
In every prayer for all of you, I pray with joy,
because you've partnered with me in sharing the Good News from the first day until now.
I'm confident that the one who began a good work in you will carry it through to completion on the day of Christ Jesus.
It's right for me to feel this way about all of you, because I hold you in my heart. Whether I'm in chains or defending and confirming the Good News, you all share in God's grace with me.
God is my witness how deeply I miss all of you with the affection of Christ Jesus.
Here's what I pray: that your love will keep growing in knowledge and every kind of insight,
so you can recognize what really matters and be sincere and blameless for the day of Christ,
filled with the fruit of righteousness that comes through Jesus Christ, to God's praise and glory.
Brothers and sisters, I want you to know that what happened to me has actually helped the Good News move forward.
My imprisonment for Christ has become clear to the whole palace guard and everyone else.
Because I'm in chains, most of the believers have become more confident in the Lord and are much bolder to speak God's word without fear.
Some preach Christ out of envy and rivalry, while others do it with good intentions.
The first group preaches Christ from selfish ambition, not sincerely. They think they can make my imprisonment more painful.
The others preach from love, knowing that I'm here to defend the Good News.
So what does it matter? Either way, whether their motives are false or genuine, Christ is being announced, and that makes me glad. Yes, I'll keep rejoicing,
because I know this will lead to my deliverance through your prayers and the help of the Spirit of Jesus Christ.
I eagerly hope and expect that I won't be put to shame in any way. Instead, with full courage, now as always, Christ will be honored in my body, whether I live or die.
For me, living means Christ, and dying is gain.
But if I continue to live in this body, my work will produce fruit. I'm not sure which I should choose.
I'm pulled in both directions. I want to leave this life and be with Christ, which would be far better,
but staying in this body is more necessary for your sake.
Since I'm convinced of this, I know I'll stay and continue with all of you, to help you grow and find joy in the faith,
so that when I'm with you again, you'll have even more reason to take pride in Christ Jesus because of me.

Whatever happens, live in a way worthy of Christ's Good News. Then, whether I come to see you or remain away, I'll hear that you stand firm in one spirit, working side by side with one purpose for the faith of the Good News.
Don't be frightened by your opponents in any way. Your courage is a sign of their destruction, and of your salvation—and this comes from God.
God has graciously given you the privilege not only of believing in Christ but also of suffering for him.
You're facing the same struggle you saw me have, and now hear that I still have.
So if there is any encouragement in Christ, any comfort from love, any sharing in the Spirit, any tenderness or compassion,
then make my joy complete: be united in purpose, share the same love, and be one in heart and mind.
Don't act out of selfish ambition or vanity. Instead, be humble and consider others more important than yourselves.
Each of you should look out not only for your own interests but also for the interests of others.
Adopt the same attitude as Christ Jesus:
Though he existed in God's form, he didn't treat equality with God as something to exploit.
Instead, he emptied himself, taking the form of a servant and becoming like human beings.
When he appeared as a human, he humbled himself and obeyed all the way to death—even death on a cross.
Because of this, God raised him to the highest place and gave him the name above every name,
so that at Jesus' name every knee will bow—in heaven, on earth, and under the earth—
and every tongue will confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
So then, my dear friends, just as you always obeyed—not only when I was with you, but even more now that I'm away—keep living out your salvation with reverence and humility.
God is the one working in you, giving you both the desire and the ability to do what pleases him.
Do everything without grumbling or arguing,
so you can be blameless and sincere, God's children without fault in a twisted and crooked generation. Then you'll shine among them like stars in the sky,
as you hold firmly to the word of life. Then on Christ's day I'll have reason to be proud that I didn't run or work for nothing.
Even if I'm being poured out like a drink offering over the sacrifice and service of your faith, I'm glad and rejoice with all of you.
In the same way, you should be glad and rejoice with me.
I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, so I'll be encouraged when I hear how you're doing.
I have no one else like him who will genuinely care about your situation.
Everyone else looks out for their own interests, not for those of Jesus Christ.
But you know Timothy's proven character. He served with me in the work of the Good News like a son working alongside his father.
So I hope to send him as soon as I know what will happen with me.
And I'm confident in the Lord that I'll come soon too.
I thought it necessary to send Epaphroditus back to you. He's my brother, co-worker, and fellow soldier, and he is your messenger who helped meet my needs.
He has been longing to see you all and was distressed because you heard he was sick.
He really was sick—almost to the point of death. But God showed mercy to him, and not only to him but also to me, so I wouldn't have one sorrow piled on another.
So I'm sending him back as soon as I can, so you'll be glad to see him again and I'll have less sorrow.
Welcome him in the Lord with great joy, and honor people like him.
He came close to death for the work of Christ, risking his life to make up for the help you couldn't give me in person.
Finally, my brothers and sisters, celebrate in the Lord! It doesn't bother me to repeat myself, and it keeps you safe.
Watch out for the dogs, those people who do evil, those who insist on physical circumcision.
We are the true circumcision—we worship by God's Spirit, celebrate in Christ Jesus, and put no confidence in human effort.
Even though I could have confidence in human credentials. If anyone thinks they have a reason to trust in them, I have even more:
I was circumcised on the eighth day, I'm from Israel and the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew born of Hebrews. As for the law, I was a Pharisee;
as for zeal, I persecuted the church; as for righteousness based on the law, I was blameless.
But whatever used to count as a gain for me, I now consider a loss because of Christ.
More than that, I consider everything a loss compared with the priceless value of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord. I gave up everything for him and consider it garbage, so I can gain Christ
and be found in him—not with my own righteousness from the law, but with the righteousness that comes through faith in Christ, the righteousness from God based on faith.
I want to know Christ, the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, becoming like him in his death,
so that somehow I may reach the resurrection from the dead.
I'm not saying I've already received this or become perfect, but I keep pursuing it to take hold of what Christ Jesus took hold of me for.
Brothers and sisters, I don't consider myself to have taken hold of it yet. But this one thing I do: I forget what is behind and reach forward to what lies ahead.
I keep moving toward the finish line to win the prize God called me to receive in Christ Jesus.
So all of us who are mature should think this way. And if you think differently about anything, God will make that clear to you too.
In any case, let's keep living by the truth we've already reached.
Brothers and sisters, join in following my example. Watch those who live by the pattern we gave you.
Many live as enemies of Christ's cross. I've often warned you about them, and now I say it with tears.
Their end is destruction; their god is their appetite; they're proud of what should shame them, and their minds are set on earthly things.
But our citizenship is in heaven, and we eagerly wait for a Savior from there, the Lord Jesus Christ.
He will transform our humble bodies to be like his glorious body, by the power that lets him bring everything under his rule.
So then, my dear brothers and sisters, whom I love and miss, my joy and crown—stand firm in the Lord this way, dear friends.
I urge Euodia and Syntyche to agree with each other in the Lord.
Yes, my true partner, please help these women. They worked hard alongside me in the Good News, together with Clement and my other co-workers, whose names are in the book of life.
Celebrate in the Lord always! I'll say it again: celebrate!
Let everyone see your gentleness. The Lord is near.
Don't be anxious about anything. In everything, bring your requests to God through prayer and petition, with thanksgiving.
Then God's peace, which is beyond all understanding, will guard your hearts and minds in Christ Jesus.
Finally, brothers and sisters, whatever is true, honorable, right, pure, lovely, admirable—if anything is excellent or worthy of praise—think about these things.
Put into practice what you learned, received, heard, and saw in me. Then the God of peace will be with you.
I was so glad in the Lord that your concern for me has finally come alive again. You always cared, but you didn't have a chance to show it.
I'm not saying this because I need anything. I've learned to be content in whatever situation I'm in.
I know how to live with little, and I know how to live with plenty. I've learned the secret of facing any circumstance, whether I'm full or hungry, whether I have plenty or need.
I can do all things through Christ, who gives me strength.
Still, you did well to share in my trouble.
You Philippians know that in the early days of the Good News, when I left Macedonia, no church partnered with me in giving and receiving except you.
Even when I was in Thessalonica, you sent help for my needs more than once.
I'm not looking for a gift. I'm looking for the fruit that increases to your account.
I have everything I need and more. I'm well supplied, now that I've received from Epaphroditus what you sent—a sweet-smelling offering, a sacrifice God accepts and enjoys.
My God will meet all your needs from his glorious riches in Christ Jesus.
To our God and Father be glory forever and ever! Amen.
Give my greetings to every one of God's holy people in Christ Jesus. The brothers and sisters with me send their greetings.
All God's people here send you greetings, especially those who belong to Caesar's household.
May the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
